Convert BLASTr results to the long format

Source: R/blast_hits.R
as_blast_long.Rd

Turns wide BLASTr results (one row per sequence, hits 1_ to n_, from any version, including k_indentity) into the long format of parallel_blast(), ranking the hits with the same rules, so that old results can be read with blast_summary() and get_tax() without running BLAST again. The BLAST order is taken from k_blast_rank or, in older results, from k. Long results are returned as they are.

Usage

as_blast_long(
  x,
  rank_by = c("similarity", "identity", "bitscore"),
  tolerance = 0.5,
  perc_qcov_hsp = 80,
  uninformative = NULL
)

Arguments

x

BLASTr results, wide or long. The sequence is in Sequence (or sequence).

rank_by, tolerance

As in check_hits().

perc_qcov_hsp

Coverage under which a hit is flagged low_qcov.

uninformative

NULL (default) keeps the flags informative of x (NA, not evaluated, when x has none; ranked as informative); a table of uninformative_references() flags the hits again with it, and ranks them among the informative ones, as parallel_blast() does.

Value

Long results (see parallel_blast()), with all the hits of x.

See also

Other result functions: blast_lca(), blast_summary(), check_hits(), similarity_score(), uninformative_references()

Examples

wide <- data.frame(
  Sequence = "ACGT", `1_subject` = "A1", `1_indentity` = 99, `1_qcovhsp` = 100,
  `1_staxid` = "9606", `2_subject` = "A2", `2_indentity` = 100,
  `2_qcovhsp` = 100, `2_staxid` = "9598", check.names = FALSE
)
as_blast_long(wide)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 25
#>   Sequence  rank tie   at_best low_qcov informative uninformative_category
#>   <chr>    <int> <lgl> <lgl>   <lgl>    <lgl>       <chr>                 
#> 1 ACGT         1 FALSE TRUE    FALSE    NA          NA                    
#> 2 ACGT         2 FALSE FALSE   FALSE    NA          NA                    
#> # ℹ 18 more variables: blast_rank <int>, subject <chr>, `subject header` <chr>,
#> #   staxid <chr>, identity <dbl>, `Similarity score` <dbl>, qcovhsp <dbl>,
#> #   nident <dbl>, length <dbl>, mismatches <dbl>, gaps <dbl>,
#> #   `query start` <dbl>, `query end` <dbl>, `subject start` <dbl>,
#> #   `subject end` <dbl>, `subject strand` <chr>, `e-value` <dbl>,
#> #   bitscore <dbl>
